For this study, we focus on the PFMS control actions for the following: • Responding to a grid request of active power dispatch from the BESS units • Isolating the data center power system from the grid (also referred to as islanding) in case of unsta- ble grid conditions • Reconnecting the data center to the grid when the voltage or frequency disturbance has subsided. For simplicity, note that in this study we do not consider reactive power dispatch, but it can be included in the same framework. In addition, generators are not used to respond to the dispatch requests from the utility, but rather they are used by the PFMS solely to provide backup power to the data center in case of an extended outage (after the BESS units have reached their predefined minimum SOC). Next, we define algorithms for the PFMS to accomplish these scenarios by testing on the Vulcan platform. Note that these algorithms are not the only way to accomplish the desired functionalities, and Vulcan provides the flexibility to test other algorithms in the future. 1. Grid-connected operation: When the grid voltage and frequency are within an acceptable range (as defined by IEEE 1547-2018), the PFMS operates the data center with power from the grid and keeps X closed.
